name: rocinante-core
description: JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol between the Rocinante UI and the .NET core. Every params, result and notification payload is a JSON Schema (2020-12) that may reference the shared definitions in $defs. Every method that changes something takes the origin window and announces the change to every window with a notification.

system.info.description: Identifies the core and the protocol version it speaks.

diagnostics.report.description: Writes a problem seen by the interface or the host to the app's log. The message never carries the writer's text: only what failed and where.

detail.description: A stack trace or similar, if there is one.

app.start.description: What a window shows when it starts. The first window opens the file the app was launched with, or the project left open last time; later windows get the project already open. If that project cannot be opened, problem says why and the window shows the welcome screen.

preferences.update.description: Changes some of the writer's preferences; omitted ones stay as they are. Broadcasts preferences.changed.

recent.list.description: Recently opened projects, most recent first.

recent.remove.description: Removes a project from the recent list; the file is not touched. Broadcasts recent.changed.

ambience.import.description: Copies an image or a sound of the writer's into the app's data folder, so it keeps working if the original moves. The core checks the kind by the file's signature, not its extension. Broadcasts ambience.changed.

ambience.remove.description: Deletes the copy of one of the writer's own images or sounds. If the preferences used it, they stop using it and preferences.changed is broadcast too. Broadcasts ambience.changed.

place.get.description: Where the writer left the open project: document and selection. Null if unknown or that document is no longer in the work.

place.save.description: Remembers where the writer is in the open project, to come back to it next time. Not broadcast: each window keeps its own cursor.

project.create.description: Creates a new project file and opens it. Fails if a file already exists at the path. Broadcasts project.opened. Without format, the work takes suggestedFormat. The format chosen becomes the suggestion for the next work.

project.open.description: Opens an existing project file, closing the current one. Broadcasts project.opened.

project.get.description: The open project, for a window that has just started. Fails with ProjectNotOpen if there is none.

project.rename.description: Changes the title of the work. Broadcasts project.changed.

project.setFormat.description: Changes the format of the work. It becomes the suggestion for the next new work. Broadcasts project.changed.

project.manuscript.description: The chapters of the work in reading order, with their text, for the page view.

project.saveAs.description: Writes a copy of the project to a new file and continues working on the copy. Broadcasts project.opened.

book.get.description: The author, the credits and the cover of the open work.

book.update.description: Changes the author or the credits; what is left out stays. A null credits goes back to the default. Broadcasts book.changed.

book.setCover.description: Gives the book its cover image, a JPEG already reduced by the UI. Broadcasts book.changed.

book.removeCover.description: Takes the cover image away. Broadcasts book.changed.

book.cover.description: The cover image of the book, to show it in the export dialog.

export.run.description: Starts writing the chapters of the open work as a book at `path`, in the background: the work is read at once and written while other requests go on. Announces export.progress and, at the end, export.finished. Nothing is left at `path` if it fails.

project.close.description: Closes the open project. Broadcasts project.closed.

document.create.description: Adds an empty chapter or fragment at a position (or at the end). Broadcasts project.changed.

document.rename.description: Changes the title of a chapter or fragment. Broadcasts project.changed.

document.move.description: Places a document at a position among the chapters or the fragments: reorders it, or converts it if the kind changes. Broadcasts project.changed.

document.delete.description: Sends a document to the trash, keeping its text, versions and notes. Broadcasts project.changed.

document.restore.description: Brings a document back from the trash to the place it had. Broadcasts project.changed.

document.save.description: Replaces the text of a document. Saving the same text changes nothing and broadcasts nothing. Otherwise broadcasts document.changed, plus versions.changed if an automatic version became due and notes.changed if notes were anchored or loosened.

version.create.description: Saves a version of the current text, with an optional name. Broadcasts versions.changed.

version.list.description: Versions of a document, newest first, without their text.

version.get.description: A version with its text, to read it or compare it with the current one.

version.restore.description: Brings back the text of a version. The current text is saved first as a beforeRestore version (null if the text already matched). Broadcasts document.changed and versions.changed.

notes.get.description: Every note of the work: loose ideas and the notes of its documents. Leaves out deleted notes and the notes of documents in the trash.

note.create.description: Creates a note: on a document, or a loose idea of the work when documentId is null. An anchored note expects the editor to place its anchor in the text with the returned id. Broadcasts notes.changed.

anchored.description: Only a note on a document can be anchored.

note.update.description: Changes a note. Changing nothing broadcasts nothing; otherwise broadcasts notes.changed.

note.delete.description: Sets a note aside: it stops being shown, and its anchor stays hidden in the text so restoring it puts it back. Set-aside notes are deleted for good the next time the work is opened. Broadcasts notes.changed.

note.restore.description: Brings back a note that was set aside. Broadcasts notes.changed.

board.get.description: Everything the list, the cards and the board need, in one go.

board.move.description: Moves cards on the board: one dragged card or all of them after arranging. Broadcasts elements.changed.

board.mentions.description: How many times each element of the work is mentioned in the text, and in how many documents.

suggestions.get.description: Proper names repeated in the text that are not the name or an alias of any element, nor dismissed: the most repeated first, twenty at most.

suggestion.dismiss.description: Stops suggesting a name in this work, for good. Broadcasts suggestions.changed.

element.create.description: Creates an element. The UI sends the suggested attributes of its kind, empty. Without position the card goes to a free place. Broadcasts elements.changed.

element.get.description: An element with everything in it, in the work or in the trash.

element.references.description: Where an element is mentioned in the text of the work, by its name or an alias: every mention, document by document in the order of the index, with a little of the text around it.

element.update.description: Changes an element. Changing nothing broadcasts nothing; otherwise broadcasts elements.changed.

element.delete.description: Sends an element to the trash with its relationships, which stop being shown. Broadcasts elements.changed.

element.restore.description: Brings an element back from the trash, with its relationships and its place on the board. Broadcasts elements.changed.

element.readImage.description: Reads an image the writer chose, so the UI can reduce it. The core checks it is PNG, JPEG or WebP by its signature, and its size.

element.setImage.description: Gives an element its image, already reduced by the UI, and its thumbnail. Both are WebP or JPEG. Broadcasts elements.changed.

element.removeImage.description: Takes the image away from an element. Broadcasts elements.changed.

element.image.description: The image of an element, whole or as a thumbnail.

relationship.create.description: Joins two elements with a kind, or with a new own kind, optionally between two chapters. Broadcasts elements.changed.

starts.description: The chapter it starts in, or null if it holds from the start of the work.

ends.description: The chapter it ends in, or null if it holds to the end of the work.

starts.description: The chapter it starts in, or null if it holds from the start of the work.

ends.description: The chapter it ends in, or null if it holds to the end of the work.

relationship.update.description: Changes the kind of a relationship (to an existing one or a new own one), the chapters it holds between, or both. What is left out stays as it was. Broadcasts elements.changed.

starts.description: The chapter it starts in, or null if it holds from the start of the work.

ends.description: The chapter it ends in, or null if it holds to the end of the work.

starts.description: The chapter it starts in, or null if it holds from the start of the work.

ends.description: The chapter it ends in, or null if it holds to the end of the work.

starts.description: The chapter it starts in, or null if it holds from the start of the work.

ends.description: The chapter it ends in, or null if it holds to the end of the work.

relationship.delete.description: Takes a relationship away. Broadcasts elements.changed.

threads.get.description: The threads of the elements the writer chose. Until the writer chooses, the five characters mentioned the most.

threads.choose.description: The elements shown in the threads, in order. Kept in the work. Broadcasts threads.changed.

milestone.create.description: Marks what happens to an element at a paragraph of a chapter, given by its text. Broadcasts milestones.changed.

passage.description: The text of the paragraph, as it is now.

milestone.update.description: Changes what a milestone says. Broadcasts milestones.changed.

dictionary.get.description: The writer's own dictionary: words the spelling check accepts in every work, in order.

dictionary.add.description: Adds a word to the writer's own dictionary. Broadcasts dictionary.changed.

dictionary.remove.description: Takes a word out of the writer's own dictionary. Broadcasts dictionary.changed.

squire.settings.description: How the squire is set up: provider, model, whether there is a key, whether it reads this work, and how it is doing.

squire.configure.description: Chooses the provider and the model. Broadcasts squire.changed.

squire.setKey.description: Keeps the API key of a provider in the system's credential store; it is never returned. Broadcasts squire.changed.

squire.forgetKey.description: Takes the API key of a provider out of the system's credential store. Broadcasts squire.changed.

squire.test.description: Asks the chosen provider something small, to see that the key and the model work.

squire.models.description: The models of the local provider (Ollama) at an address; empty for the providers in the cloud.

squire.enable.description: Lets the squire read this work, or stops it. Broadcasts squire.changed.

squire.analyze.description: Gives the squire a paragraph the writer has just finished; it reads it in the background if it is on and the paragraph changed.

proposals.get.description: The squire's proposals waiting for the writer, the newest first.

proposal.accept.description: Makes what a proposal says, with the writer's corrections if any. Broadcasts squire.changed and elements.changed.

proposal.dismiss.description: Drops a proposal; it is not proposed again for that paragraph. Broadcasts squire.changed.

project.opened.description: A project was created, opened or saved under a new path. Every window switches to it.

project.changed.description: The title or the index of the open project changed.

project.closed.description: The open project was closed. Every window returns to the welcome screen.

document.changed.description: The text of a document changed; windows other than the origin showing it should reload it.

versions.changed.description: A version of a document was added.

notes.changed.description: Notes changed: created, edited, resolved, linked, anchored or loosened (notes), or set aside or gone with their document to the trash (removed). Each list has only what changed.

preferences.changed.description: The writer's preferences changed; every window applies them.

ambience.changed.description: The writer's own images and sounds changed.

elements.changed.description: Elements, relationships or kinds changed. Each list has only what changed: elements are now in the work, trash went to the trash; details carries the whole element when more than its summary changed.

suggestions.changed.description: A suggestion was dismissed: every window asks for them again.

dictionary.changed.description: The writer's own dictionary changed: every window checks the spelling with these words.

squire.changed.description: The squire changed: its settings or state, new proposals (proposals) or proposals no longer waiting (removed).

threads.changed.description: The writer chose other elements to show in the threads.

milestones.changed.description: Milestones were made, changed or followed their paragraph (milestones), or were removed (removed).

book.changed.description: The author, the credits or the cover of the book changed.

export.progress.description: How far an export has gone: chapters written out of all of them.

export.finished.description: An export ended: the file is at `path`, or `reason` says why there is none.

Id.description: UUID v7 in canonical lowercase form.

Timestamp.description: ISO 8601 date and time with offset.

FilePath.description: Absolute or relative path of a project file on this computer.

Title.description: Title of a project, chapter or fragment. Surrounding spaces are trimmed; blank titles are refused with titleRequired.

VersionName.description: Optional name of a manual version. Blank means no name.

NoteText.description: Plain text of a note, which the core derives from its content.

NoteElements.description: Elements a note is linked with, each once.

NoteChanges.description: The parts of a note that change; what is left out stays as it is.

Position.description: Zero-based place among the documents of one kind.

Revision.description: Monotonic counter, incremented on every change to a document's text. 0 means never edited.

WindowLabel.description: Label of the window that originated a change.

ErrorReason.description: Value of error.data.reason for ProjectNotOpen, RuleViolated and ProjectFileProblem errors. The UI turns each one into a message in Spanish.

Theme.description: paper: ivory paper. candlelight: warm dark.

OutlineMode.description: Whether the index is docked to the side or floats over the text.

mentionsVisible.description: Whether the mentions of the fichas are marked in the text.

correctionVisible.description: Whether the spelling and punctuation marks show in the text.

checkForUpdates.description: Whether Rocinante looks on GitHub for a new version when a work opens. Off, it never connects on its own.

AmbienceId.description: A background or an ambient sound: builtin:<name> for one that comes with the app, own:<id> for one the writer added. The list of built-in ones lives in the UI; one that no longer exists is shown as the default.

Typing.description: The sound of each keystroke that writes. muted keeps the choice and the volume.

Ambient.description: One looping ambient sound in the mix, at its own level.

SessionGoal.description: What the writer aims for in one session of focus mode: nothing, new words, or minutes.

Ambience.description: The writer's focus mode and sounds: the background behind the sheet, the typing sound, the ambient mix, dimming the other paragraphs and the session goal. Ambients may not repeat (ambientRepeated); an own: id must exist (ambienceNotFound).

OwnAmbienceKind.description: image: a background. sound: an ambient sound.

OwnAmbience.description: An image or a sound the writer added. file is the copy in the app's data folder, the only place the UI may read it from; name is the original file name, shown to the writer.

Place.description: A document and a ProseMirror selection in it.

exists.description: Whether the file is still there; the welcome screen dims missing ones.

StartState.description: defaultFolder is where new projects are proposed: Documents/Rocinante. suggestedFormat is the format of the last work the writer set up, or the default one, offered for the next new work. ownAmbience lists the images and sounds the writer added.

Statistics.description: Counts shown to the writer. Notes never count.

DocumentEntry.description: A chapter or fragment as the index shows it.

ProjectIndex.description: Chapters in reading order, fragments in drawer order, and the trash, most recent first.

ProjectState.description: The open project: its file, title, index, format, and the counts of every chapter outside the trash (work).

VersionSummary.description: A version as listed, without its text.

documentId.description: Null for a loose idea of the work.

anchored.description: False when the anchored passage was deleted, or for a loose idea.

order.description: Place of the note's anchor among the anchors of its document's text, from the last save of the text; null when it is not anchored or its anchor has not been saved yet.

DocumentChange.description: Params of a change to one document of the index.

DocumentReference.description: Params of a query about one document.

TipTapDocument.description: Root of a TipTap/ProseMirror document as produced by editor.getJSON().

TipTapNode.description: Any TipTap node. Node-specific shapes are validated by the editor schema, not here.

DiagnosticSource.description: Who saw the problem: the interface of a window, or the host that runs the windows and the core.

PageSize.description: The named sizes the writer can pick, or custom. pocket: 11 × 17 cm. digest: 5.5 × 8.5 in. trade: 6 × 9 in. The name is a label: the measures are always in the format.

Typeface.description: The typefaces bundled with the app for the text of the work.

Millimetres.description: A length on the page, in millimetres.

WorkFormat.description: How the work is set: the page of the book it will be, its margins and its type. Pages are 70 to 300 mm a side, the body 8 to 16 pt and the leading 1 to 2 (formatOutOfRange), and the margins must leave a text area of at least 40 × 60 mm (textAreaTooSmall).

pageWidth.description: Width of the page, in millimetres.

pageHeight.description: Height of the page, in millimetres.

bodySize.description: Size of the text, in points.

leading.description: Line height as a multiple of the body size.

firstLineIndent.description: Indent the first line of each paragraph that follows another.

justified.description: Justified text; otherwise aligned to the left.

dropCap.description: A drop cap at the start of each chapter.

Manuscript.description: The text of the book: the chapters in reading order. Fragments and the trash are not part of it.

ElementKind.description: What an element of the work is. other carries a kind named by the writer in otherKind.

ElementName.description: Name of an element. Surrounding spaces are trimmed; a blank name is refused with nameRequired.

OtherKindName.description: The kind of an element of kind other, as the writer names it: object, faction, era…

ElementAliases.description: Other names of an element. Blank ones are dropped.

ElementAttributes.description: Name–value pairs of an element, in the order the writer gave them.

BoardPosition.description: Where a card sits on the board, in board units.

ElementImageInfo.description: An element has an image. version changes with every new image, so the UI knows when its copy is stale.

ElementSummary.description: What the list and the board show of an element.

Element.description: An element with everything the writer put in it.

ElementChanges.description: The parts of an element that change; what is left out stays as it is. otherKind goes with kind other and is null otherwise.

RelationshipKindId.description: A kind of relationship: builtin:<name> for a common one, whose words live in the UI, or own:<id> for one the writer wrote in this work.

RelationshipLabel.description: How a relationship reads from one side: «hijo de». Surrounding spaces are trimmed.

NewRelationshipKind.description: A kind of relationship the writer writes. Without inverse it is symmetric: it reads the same from both sides.

RelationshipKind.description: A kind of relationship the writer wrote in this work.

Relationship.description: Two elements joined by a kind. It reads forward from `from` and inverse from `to`. It holds between the chapters `starts` and `ends`, both included; without them, in the whole work.

starts.description: The chapter it starts in, or null if it holds from the start of the work.

ends.description: The chapter it ends in, or null if it holds to the end of the work.

Board.description: Every element of the work, its relationships and the writer's kinds of relationship. Relationships of elements in the trash are left out.

ImageData.description: The bytes of an image in base64, with their type.

chapters.description: Documents with at least one mention.

first.description: The first mention in the order of the index, or null if there is none.

documents.description: Only the documents with mentions, in the order of the index: chapters, then fragments.

together.description: The other elements mentioned in the same paragraphs, the most paragraphs first.

Mention.description: One mention: its place among the mentions of the element in its document, and the text around it.

DictionaryWord.description: A word, as written, without spaces.

hasKey.description: Whether the chosen provider has a key in the system's store.

enabled.description: Whether the squire reads the open work.

ProposalChanges.description: What the writer corrected before accepting; what is left out stays as proposed.

MilestoneText.description: What happens to an element at a passage, in a short sentence. Surrounding spaces are trimmed; a blank one is refused with milestoneTextRequired.

Milestone.description: Something that happens to an element at a paragraph of a chapter. It follows its paragraph as the text changes; when the paragraph is gone it stays in its chapter, lost.

passage.description: The paragraph it belongs to, as it was last found.

lost.description: Whether its paragraph is no longer in the chapter.

Threads.description: The threads of the chosen elements through the chapters of the work, in the order of the index.

chosen.description: The elements shown, in the order the writer chose them.

chapters.description: The chapters of the work in reading order. Fragments have no place in the story.

threads.description: One per chosen element: the chapters where it is mentioned, and how many times.

meetings.description: Two chosen elements mentioned in the same paragraphs of a chapter, and in how many.

milestones.description: The milestones of the chosen elements, chapter by chapter and in the order of the text.

AuthorName.description: The name of the author as it goes on the cover: a name or a pen name. Surrounding spaces are trimmed; it may be empty.

CreditsText.description: The text of the credits page, as the author writes it, in lines.

BookDetails.description: What the book carries besides the text of the work: its author, its credits and, for EPUB, a cover image.

credits.description: The credits as the author wrote them, or null for the default: «© {year} {author}. Todos los derechos reservados.».

cover.description: The cover image, a JPEG reduced by the UI, or null.

ExportParts.description: The parts the book carries besides the chapters.

cover.description: The title page, with the title and the author; in EPUB also the cover image, if any.
